topics.title: Pre-RFC Discussion: Activating the Nervos DAO Treasury

recent_posts.topic_title: Pre-RFC Discussion: Activating the Nervos DAO Treasury
recent_posts.author: phroi
recent_posts.content_text:
Thanks @chenyukang for sharing the Optimistic Tally!! An overview:
A proposal is a Type ID cell holding a bond.
Vote cells reference the voter’s DAO deposits, which must be older than the proposal. Weight is the deposits’ capacity.
Counting cells certify YES votes in slices of voters, split by lock hash prefix. After the voting period, the proposer finalizes the proposal with at least yes_threshold YES votes.
During the challenge period anyone can challenge with certified NO votes. If NO votes are at least YES votes, the proposal is rejected and the challenger takes the bond. Otherwise it passes.
An administrator config cell sets all parameters, can halt the system and can veto finalized proposals.
Sums are checked on-chain. Nothing proves that every vote was counted, but each side has a reason to certify its own votes. Compared with the other non-ZK designs:
DAO v1.1 tallies off-chain. Optimistic Tally checks eligibility and sums on-chain.
Deposit-Paired Voting (mine) parks deposits under voting logic for an exact tally with revotes, at the cost of migrating deposits and one shared cell. Optimistic Tally reads deposits once, when the vote is cast: they must predate the proposal but need not stay deposited.
CKB Governance by @anihdev is the closest relative: its tally lanes are like the lock-hash slices. Optimistic Tally adds the bond and challenge. It weighs votes by DAO deposits instead of one per wallet.
I’ll be sure to open my questions / doubts on GitHub!
Keep up the Great Work and congratulations on joining CKBA, glad to see your hard work recognized!!
Phroi

recent_posts.topic_title: [DIS] Hardening Kirea Finance (Native RWA Lending on CKB)
recent_posts.author: truthixify
recent_posts.content_text:
Can you clarify how this proposal fits alongside your active Tranfr — Programmable Recovery for CKB - #6 by tianji Spark grant?
Tranfr has received its initial payment and still has the recovery path, SDK, frontend, and documentation outstanding, while Kirea is another solo 10-week commitment. The scopes appear separate but the overlapping timeline and delivery capacity should be disclosed. Would Kirea begin only after Tranfr is completed and accepted?

recent_posts.topic_title: [DIS] Hardening Kirea Finance (Native RWA Lending on CKB)
recent_posts.author: SalmanDev
recent_posts.content_text:
Thank you for raising this important question.
To clarify:
Tranfr Timeline: Tranfr (my second project under the Spark program) is already well underway and will be fully completed, wrapped up, and ready for acceptance within the next two weeks.
Proven Execution Capacity: In fact, I was able to build the complete working MVP for Kirea Finance while concurrently pushing updates and delivering on Tranfr, which demonstrates my ability to manage multiple workflows efficiently.
Sequential Focus: Now that the core prototype for Kirea is built, its heavy hardening and integration phase will kick off seamlessly as Tranfr reaches its final completion stage.
Previous Experience: Having successfully delivered my previous project under the Nervos Spark program (the Stripe-Style React Payment Library for Fiber Network), I am very comfortable pacing deliverables effectively. That project was delivered ahead of schedule.
Tranfr will be completely out the door within the next two weeks before Kirea hits its major milestone execution. I appreciate you keeping me accountable on delivery bandwidth.
